newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINVEST SAYS TO REMAIN BIG POYRY OWNER.
newsitem.headline: FINVEST SAYS TO REMAIN BIG POYRY OWNER.

text.p: Finnish capacitor and engineering group Finvest will continue to be a major owner of Jaakko Poyry even if it lists the company and sells some shares, Finvest chief executive Niilo Pellonmaa said on Thursday.

"I want to emphasise that we do not plan to give up our entire stake (in Jaakko Poyry), in any case we will remain an important owner and of course we believe in Poyry's business," Pellonmaa told Reuters by telephone.
Finvest earlier said it was investigating listing its wholly owned forestry engineering and consulting unit Jaakko Poyry Group on the Helsinki and Stockholm bourses.
Pellonmaa declined to say how large a stake Finvest would retain. A decision on the listing could be expected in autumn.

"The preparations will take a few months, and after that we could be ready to move at any time ... so I would say from about the end of September we could be ready to go to the market in a matter of weeks," Pellonmaa said.
"Jaakko Poyry has always been very big in Sweden ... both markets are very important to us," Pellonmaa said, adding that for the time being the company had no plans to seek bourse listings elsewhere.

Finvest said in a statement that Poyry's business operations developed better than planned in the first four months of the year, though net sales fell to 414.4 million from 437.6 million a year earlier.
Its January-April operating profit rose to 31.3 million from 29.4 million, and the orderstock was 735.8 million, compared with 688.1 million in the year-ago period.
